abstract: Metabolite dynamics remain difficult to visualize in living systems, particularly for nucleotide sugars that link metabolism to glycosylation and signaling. Here we repurpose Helicobacter pylori UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase to develop UGluS, a genetically encoded ratiometric fluorescent sensor for its biosynthetic product, UDP-glucose (UDP-Glc). Circularly permuted GFP insertion and directed evolution yield an approximately 18-fold excitation-ratio response and an apparent dissociation constant of 32.5 M, with preferential responsiveness to UDP-Glc over related metabolites. Live-cell imaging and microplate assays reveal responses to metabolic, genetic and mechanosensitive perturbations in mammalian cells. In zebrafish larvae, UGluS reveals uridine-induced increases in UDP-Glc availability and fin-fold enrichment. In mouse liver slices and skeletal muscle in vivo, insulin- and glucose-induced decreases in UDP-Glc availability accompany increased glycogen content. These findings establish UGluS as a tool for imaging UDP-Glc dynamics across biological scales and extend the use of biosynthetic enzymes as fluorescent sensing scaffolds.
